gaps.sentence: She ___ very well in her end-of-year exams.
gaps.hint: collocation: to ___ well in an exam
gaps.explanation: do well in an exam is the standard phrase meaning to perform successfully.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ losses of two million last year.
We ___ breakfast on the terrace every morning in summer.
gaps.explanation: have breakfast/lunch/dinner is the standard collocation for eating meals.

gaps.sentence: The newspapers ___ the story about the minister's resignation.
gaps.hint: collocation with 'a story' meaning revealed it first
gaps.explanation: break a story is the journalism collocation meaning to be the first to report news.

gaps.sentence: The roads were almost empty — the traffic was surprisingly ___.
gaps.explanation: light traffic means few vehicles on the road; its opposite is heavy traffic.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her breath before diving into the pool.
gaps.explanation: 'Hold one's breath' — catching breath is recovering it afterwards.

gaps.sentence: We ___ our shopping at the local market every Saturday.
gaps.explanation: do the shopping is the collocation for buying food and household goods.

gaps.sentence: A true friend will always ___ a secret.
gaps.explanation: keep a secret is the fixed collocation for not telling it to anyone.
